episode.summary:
The 1960s were when Heinlein produced some of his most famous works. And they started to bring him fame outside the Science Fiction community, which was most unusual.

Heinlein in the 1960s

Heinlein had interests that he tended to keep hidden in the early years while he was establishing himself as a writer, particularly as he was feeding the lucrative Juvenile market. notes.summary: This episode explores Robert A. Heinlein's major works from the 1960s, a decade when he gained mainstream fame and openly expressed his views on politics, religion, and sexuality. Key novels discussed include Stranger in a Strange Land, Podkayne of Mars, Warfins of the Sky, Glory Road, Farnham's Freehold, and The Moon is a Harsh Mistress. The episode highlights themes of societal critique, libertarianism, and speculative fiction, noting awards and cultural impact. Fans of classic science fiction and literary analysis will appreciate this overview.
